chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When a free man, a slave, and a polytheist have intercourse with one woman in one pure period, and they claim the child, a lot is drawn between them, and the child belongs to the one whose lot comes out.

key_terms.أُقْرِعَ: A lot was drawn / Drawing lots

ai.seo_question: How is paternity determined when multiple men claim a child from one woman in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Kafi illustrates the Shia juristic application of qara' (drawing lots) to resolve paternity disputes when multiple men of varying statuses—free, slave, or polytheist—intercourse with the same woman during a single pure period. Unlike the Sunni view which often prioritizes the free man, Shia scholarship emphasizes the equal probabilistic weight of the claimants in this specific scenario, reflecting a pragmatic approach to lineage preservation. The hadith underscores the importance of clear evidentiary mechanisms in Islamic family law to prevent ambiguity in inheritance and marital rights.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, and Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>) having said:

‘When the free man and the slave and the Polytheist fall with one woman in one pure period, so the child is claimed for, a lot would be drawn between them, and the child would be for the one whose arrow (lot) comes out’.
